issues.description: The supplied package inventory contains the driver, documentation, historical log and two identifier lists, but none of the analysis/preparation DTA inputs. The driver consumes many separate provider, calendar, financial, social-tie, event and visit-text tables; fields, keys, period coverage and construction are incompletely documented. The identifier lists are not the analysis panel.

Several exact files are consumed without an in-driver producer, including annual/semiannual report visit-week tables, lookup/calendar tables, school and underwriter link panels, event-week tables, and report-text/fund visit inputs. Obtain the author-prepared files or their complete field, key, period and construction handoffs; do not infer that these are generated by the supplied script.
The Stata driver starts by changing into an absolute author-machine volume path. Select a portable working-copy root so relative reads and outputs resolve in an isolated project directory.

The first use of 财务数据_new.dta is at line 233, while the supplied driver writes it later at line 606. A fresh line-1-to-end invocation therefore cannot rely on that output at its first consumer. The existing lines 577–606 are the supported producer block and use five separate financial inputs; run that block first as a conditional bootstrap stage after those inputs are supplied, then retain and execute the complete driver.

evidence.quote:
Public Disclosure of Private Meetings: Does Observing Peers’ Information
                 Acquisition Affect Analysts’ Attention Allocation?

evidence.description: The datasheet names the vendor and report sources used for site visits and forecasts.
evidence.quote:
We obtained the data from a variety of sources, including China Stock Market & Accounting
Research Database (CSMAR), Chinese Research Data Services (CNRDS), RESSET, and
Corporate Site Visit Database (CSVD) developed by Datago Technology Limited. In addition, for
site visits before 2012, we also hand collect site visit records from firm semi-annual and quarterly
reports that are not disclosed in the annual reports.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes CSMAR site visits after July 2012 and firm and analyst characteristics.
evidence.quote:
CSMAR data
We use the data on corporate site visits after July 2012 from CSMAR, which collects the records
of site visits from the HudongYi platform. We also use the data on firm characteristics and analyst
characteristics from CSMAR. We downloaded the CSMAR data in July 2019. In addition, we use
the data from CSMAR combined with analyst reports and web search to construct the indicator

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies the three forecast sources and the pre-2012 CSVD and hand-collected visit records.
evidence.quote:
CNRDS data and RESSET data
We use analyst forecast data from three databases: CSMAR, CNRDS, and RESSET. We
downloaded CNRDS and RESSET data from June 2019 to August 2020.

CSVD data
We use the data on corporate site visits before July 2012 from CSVD, which collects the records
of site visits disclosed in firms’ periodic reports. We downloaded the CSVD data in August 2020.
In addition, for site visits before 2012, we also hand collect site visit records from firm semi-annual
and quarterly reports that are not disclosed in the annual reports.

* Adjust broker names *

gen amount_length=strlen(name)
bysort name: gen total1=_N

gen rptdt= date(报告公布日, "YMD")
format rptdt %td
format rptdt %tdCCYY-NN-DD

drop if EPS==.

actions.description: Obtain or stage the exact author-prepared inputs consumed by the driver, with documented source-to-file mappings and field/key/period contracts for each independent table. Preserve the current source-specific forecast, visit, control, event and supporting stages.
steps: Request or obtain the three cleaned forecast-provider files separately, plus the annual actual-EPS, opening-price and analyst-report-week lookups; document the common columns, identifier crosswalk, periods and forecast-year alignment.

Request the prepared broker-named visit panel and the separate annual and semiannual/quarterly report inputs; retain the distinct annual/semiannual weekly tables and specify source dates, duplicate/overlap rules and the post-2012 CSMAR versus earlier CSVD handoff.
Provide the week/year-week/shifted-week/quarter calendars and stock reference table, including the date keys and trading/fiscal-week conventions used by the Stata merges.

Provide each accounting, volume, shares, ownership, SOE, industry and daily return input with definitions, units, firm/date keys and complete required history; identify the actual table mappings for each named file.

Provide the analyst ranking, school/underwriter/city link inputs, uncertain-visit samples, four event-week tables, report-level text-detail/length tables and fund visit table with their producer or source specifications.

For each file without an in-driver producer, supply the exact author-prepared version or the missing upstream preparation steps. Do not substitute identifiers, guessed data or unrelated catalog candidates.
Provide the non-clean firm-year update table 不干净id_year_updated.dta or identify its upstream producer, meaning, keys and coverage.
validation: After authorized files are staged, use bounded format-aware metadata/readability checks and compare each table separately with the consumed field names and join keys documented in the driver.
Verify each required date/security range and author-prepared transformation from source documentation; a one-row read or catalog count does not establish historical or population coverage.
Trace every externally prepared table to its producer and confirm that the stage order satisfies its consumers before a later authorized full run.

actions.description: After the separately documented input, project-root and Stata add-on prerequisites are complete, build the financial-control panel before its first use, then run the complete supplied Stata workflow.
steps: Complete A_INPUT_CONTRACTS_AND_STAGING, A_PORTABLE_ROOT and A_STATA_ADDON_SETUP in an isolated working copy first; resolve the 47 distinct input contracts and the required runtime setup before this sequence.

Before the first top-to-bottom pass through code_RZZ.do, run its existing financial-control block at lines 577–606 from the selected project root. This block reads the five separately required files Asset_Leverage.dta, ROA.dta, MB_Q.dta, tradingVol.dta and sharesn.dta, then writes 财务数据_new.dta for the earlier consumer at line 233.

After that generated panel is present, run the complete, unabridged code_RZZ.do from line 1 in Stata batch mode from the same root. Keep every author stage and branch, including the later lines 577–606 rebuild and all subsequent tables, robustness checks, social-tie, event, text-length and fund branches.

Do not claim that a single cold top-to-bottom pass can satisfy the first line-233 use before the later line-606 producer. Do not remove, reorder, substitute, or redesign any analysis branch; if the conditional bootstrap stage cannot be executed as supplied, request author clarification before running the full script.
Retain the comprehensive log and generated table files in the working copy for later review.
validation: Before running the bootstrap block, verify the five input tables and their required join keys/fields have been supplied and staged; confirm the block creates 财务数据_new.dta before line 233 is reached.

During the subsequent full run, confirm the first line-233 consumer succeeds from the bootstrap output and record the effect of the later in-script rebuild at lines 577–606 without assuming byte identity.
Use the full log to confirm every code-defined table, robustness, social-tie, event, text-length and fund branch remains in the executed workflow and its expected outputs are captured.

review_notes: This is a cumulative update to the populated stage-one draft; the exact prior bytes are preserved read-only at probes/draft_checkpoint_stage1.json.
All 38 frozen dependency IDs are mapped. Ten are direct external inputs and twenty-eight are generated by the supplied Stata driver; generated classifications cite both producer and consumer lines.

The input requirements include direct table reads beyond the dependency checklist, including separate annual/semiannual visit-week tables, week/calendar maps, social-tie panels, report/event inputs, visit text and fund records.

The two packaged DTA files are readable identifier lists (4,003 analyst identifiers and 814 firm identifiers); they do not replace the absent analysis/preparation input tables and are not read by code_RZZ.do.

Official CSMAR/CNRDS/RESSET pages and local catalog searches are candidate discovery evidence only. No public route is marked verified; no product entitlement, source-to-file mapping, field contract or coverage is inferred from a provider name or a generic landing page.
Only code_RZZ.do, its documentation, registered metadata, bounded helper probes and named catalog/public metadata were reviewed. No author workflow was executed.

The screened full read/write inventory also surfaced 不干净id_year_updated.dta as an external id/year input outside the frozen dependency checklist; it is retained as an additional unresolved requirement rather than treated as generated.

D0003 is an out-of-order generated edge: the driver first reads 财务数据_new.dta at line 233 and only writes it at line 606. The existing lines 577–606 provide the supported conditional bootstrap using five separately identified inputs; a fresh single top-to-bottom run is not claimed to satisfy this first use.
